title: OpenAI’s head of ethics leaves less than a year after joining
titleZh: OpenAI 的道德主管在加入后不到一年就离职
author: ilamont
relevanceReason: 命中 2 个 AI/科技关键词。

comments.author: seanhunter
comments.textRawHtml:
Organisationally it never works to have a group whose only job is to say no to some other group. The incentives are diametrically opposed and as a structure it can’t last.

If you had an AI company and want it to be ethical you have to find a way to make ethics everyone’s responsibility, and have the consequences of poor ethics bite the people who make those bad decisions. If you just outsource it to the ethics group what happens is

1)everyone else thinks they don’t need to worry about ethics

2)the ethics group need to justify their existence so introduce a bunch of guidelines that everyone initially thinks are reasonable but over time people think are increasingly out of touch

3) The ethics group start to “make difficult calls” and say no to things. Initially everyone supports this and feels like the system is working as it should but over time everyone starts to just see them as an obstacle to work around

4)everyone else starts to try to work around what the ethics group says

5)The ethics group grows powerless and disconnected. The people who work around them “get things done” so get promoted etc whereas they only visibly put roadblocks in peoples’ way, so they get sidelined.

6)Eventually they get disbanded with some corporate announcement thanking them for their hard work, thought leadership etc. All that has been achieved is a lot of wasted time and bad blood.
comments.textZhHtml:
从组织上讲，一个小组的唯一工作就是对其他小组说“不”，这是行不通的。 这些激励措施是截然相反的，而且作为一种结构，它无法持久。

如果你有一家人工智能公司，并希望它符合道德规范，你就必须找到一种方法，让道德规范成为每个人的责任，而糟糕的道德规范会影响到那些做出错误决定的人。 如果你只是将其外包给道德团体，会发生的情况是

1）其他人都认为他们不需要担心道德问题

2）道德团体需要证明其存在的合理性，因此引入一系列最初每个人都认为合理的指导方针，但随着时间的推移，人们认为越来越脱节

3）道德团体开始“做出艰难的决定”并对事情说不。 最初，每个人都支持这一点，并感觉系统正在按其应有的方式运行，但随着时间的推移，每个人都开始将其视为解决问题的障碍

4）其他人开始尝试解决道德团体所说的内容

5）道德团体变得无能为力且脱节。 在他们周围工作的人“把事情做好”，因此得到晋升等，而他们只是明显地在人们的道路上设置障碍，因此他们被边缘化。

6）最终，他们被解散，并发布了一些公司公告，感谢他们的辛勤工作、思想领导力等。所取得的一切都是浪费了大量的时间和不和。

children.author: plaidfuji
children.textRawHtml:
If this were true, food companies wouldn’t have a Regulatory team. Except every single one of them does, and they function similarly to how you describe, but without dissolving. They’re treated as a constraint that must be checked before major projects can advance. Sometimes they’re the longest-lead item on a new project and if you don’t get them involved early, your project can sink at a late stage after great expense.

The only difference is AI isn’t regulated, so they just have a vague “ethics” department with no real teeth because it’s essentially PR and has no legal consequences to back up their stance.
children.textZhHtml:
如果这是真的，食品公司就不会拥有监管团队。除了它们中的每一个都会这样做，而且它们的功能与您所描述的类似，但不会溶解。它们被视为一种约束，在重大项目推进之前必须对其进行检查。有时它们是新项目中周期最长的项目，如果你不尽早让他们参与，你的项目可能会在后期阶段陷入困境，付出巨大的代价。

唯一的区别是人工智能不受监管，所以他们只有一个模糊的“道德”部门，没有真正的牙齿，因为它本质上是公关，没有法律后果来支持他们的立场。

children.author: jkahrs595
children.textRawHtml:
> The only difference is AI isn’t regulated

Seems extremely obvious that this is exactly why the food industry doesn’t dissolve its regulatory team?
children.textZhHtml:
> 唯一的区别是人工智能不受监管

似乎非常明显，这正是食品行业不解散其监管团队的原因？

children.author: red-iron-pine
children.textRawHtml:
ethics isn't regulation. regulation is external, forced upon them, and has direct usually 1-to-1 consequences if you don't comply.

ethics may feed into regulation, hopefully, but the regs may just as easily give the orgs they regulate a pass on things they shouldn't; e.g. "regulatory capture".
children.textZhHtml:
道德不是监管。 监管是外部的，是强加给他们的，如果你不遵守，通常会产生一对一的直接后果。

希望道德可以融入监管，但监管可能很容易让他们监管的组织放过他们不应该做的事情；例如“监管捕获”。

children.author: hbn
children.textRawHtml:
Food companies aren't rapidly developing groundbreaking new technologies on the most competitive battleground in computing history where everyone is trying to compete globally just to create the foundational infrastructure.

It's not that hard to get some pickled eggs on a grocery store shelf while remaining compliant with expected ethical standards for the industry. Food is a pretty mature industry.
children.textZhHtml:
食品公司并没有在计算历史上竞争最激烈的战场上快速开发突破性的新技术，每个人都试图在全球范围内竞争，只是为了创建基础设施。

在杂货店货架上买到一些腌鸡蛋，同时保持符合行业预期的道德标准，这并不难。食品是一个相当成熟的行业。

if the speed comes at the cost of not making reasonable ethical considerations, is that not something that should be looked at?
children.textZhHtml:

如果速度的提高是以没有做出合理的道德考虑为代价的，这难道不是值得关注的事情吗？

children.author: MetroWind
children.textRawHtml: Of course it is. Doesn't mean the stakeholders are willing.
children.textZhHtml: 当然是。并不意味着利益相关者愿意。

children.author: SkyPuncher
children.textRawHtml:
I don’t view that team as saying “No”.

Instead, I view that team as saying “Customers expect safe food. Our job is to help you deliver on that”.
children.textZhHtml:
我不认为该团队在说“不”。

相反，我认为该团队在说“顾客期望安全的食品。我们的工作就是帮助您实现这一目标”。

children.author: k2xl
children.textRawHtml:
I don't think that's a fair comparison. Regulatory teams exist to make sure companies comply with actual laws and regulations. There's a relatively objective standard they're enforcing.

Big tech has the same thing in its legal and compliance teams, and those teams absolutely can kill projects. That's pretty different from an amorphous "ethics" committee deciding what is or isn't ethical based on much more subjective criteria.
children.textZhHtml:
我认为这是一个不公平的比较。监管团队的存在是为了确保公司遵守实际的法律法规。他们正在执行一个相对客观的标准。

大型科技公司的法律和合规团队也有同样的事情，这些团队绝对可以杀死项目。这与一个无定形的“道德”委员会根据更主观的标准来决定什么是道德的，什么是不道德的。

children.author: BloondAndDoom
children.textRawHtml: I get what you are saying but that’s exactly how security and compliance work. And I don’t think amount of people who want to be ethical in an organization ia that different than people who want to build secure software (but possibly no one gives a shit compliance other than it’s something that needs to be done)
children.textZhHtml: 我明白你的意思，但这正是安全性和合规性的工作原理。而且我认为在一个组织中想要遵守道德的人与想要构建安全软件的人并没有什么不同（但可能没有人会关心合规性，除了这是需要做的事情）

children.author: hnlmorg
children.textRawHtml:
And organisations fail at security when security and compliance is only considered important by that one teamnn

Security requires the whole business to buy in. And it requires processes that allow people to get shit done without people resorting to shadow IT; thus working around that one team.

So the GPs point still works.
children.textZhHtml:
当安全性和合规性仅被一个团队认为重要时，组织就会在安全性方面失败

安全性需要整个企业的支持。它需要允许人们在不诉诸影子 IT 的情况下完成任务的流程；从而围绕该团队开展工作。

因此 GP 点仍然有效。

children.author: ivan_gammel
children.textRawHtml: Rule number one of CIO: become friends with CFO and chief lawyer. And nothing else matters.
children.textZhHtml: CIO 的第一条规则：与 CFO 和首席律师成为朋友。其他都不重要。

children.author: close04
children.textRawHtml:
The difference between "ethics" and "security and compliance" is that the latter is something that hits inside the company, while the former usually hits outside of the company.

Poor security practices harm your teams, your data, and usually you make moderate savings at best. Poor ethics "only" harm your customers while making bank for the company.

This is the real problem with ethics in a large corporation. You're not saying "no" to another team, you're saying no to large profits, you're saying no to the company's leadership. That is what never works.
children.textZhHtml:
“道德”和“安全与合规”之间的区别在于，后者影响的是公司内部，而前者通常会影响公司外部。

不良的安全实践会损害您的团队、您的数据，而且通常您最多只能节省一些成本。不良的道德“只会”伤害你的客户，同时为公司赚钱。

这是大公司道德的真正问题。你不是对另一个团队说“不”，你是在对巨额利润说不，你是在对公司的领导层说不。 这是永远行不通的。
